label: DeFi Governance & Operational Risk Assessment
description: Assess governance and operational risk in DeFi protocols: smart-contract and oracle risk, governance-token concentration, admin keys and upgradeability, MEV, the MiCA 'sufficiently decentralised' perimeter question, and an operational-resilience lens (DORA-style). Produces a scored risk register and remediation plan for builders, DAOs, investors, and regulated firms with DeFi exposure.

claudeKnowledge.description: MiCA (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114) Recitals 22 & 75–77 on fully decentralised services; DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) ICT-risk and third-party concentration provisions; ESMA/EBA technical standards and the ESMA DeFi reports; IOSCO Policy Recommendations for DeFi (Nov 2023); FSB high-level recommendations on crypto-asset activities (July 2023); BIS/ECB DeFi and MEV research; on-chain governance data (token-holder concentration, multisig signer sets, timelock parameters); audit findings and exploit post-mortems (oracle manipulation, governance attacks, bridge hacks)

guidedInputs.label: Protocol / Structure Type
guidedInputs.description: What kind of DeFi protocol or structure is being assessed?

guidedInputs.label: Your Role / Vantage Point
guidedInputs.description: Who is commissioning this assessment? This sets which risks are actionable for you and the regulatory-attribution lens.

options.label: Core team / protocol foundation (building or operating it)
Investor / LP / treasury allocator doing diligence
Regulated firm assessing DeFi exposure (CASP, fund, bank)

guidedInputs.label: Jurisdiction(s) for the Perimeter View
guidedInputs.description: Which regulatory perimeters should the MiCA / operational-resilience analysis consider?

guidedInputs.label: Known Centralisation / Control Vectors
guidedInputs.description: Which control points exist? These drive both the operational-risk score and the MiCA 'sufficiently decentralised' perimeter question.

options.label: Upgradeable proxy contracts (admin can change logic)
Admin keys / privileged roles (pause, mint, parameter set)
No timelock / short timelock on privileged actions
Single L1/L2 or RPC / hosting concentration

guidedInputs.label: Risk Domains to Prioritise
guidedInputs.description: Which of the eight DeFi risk domains should the assessment go deep on?

options.label: Smart-contract & code risk (audits, upgradeability, formal verification)
Economic / market risk (liquidity, depeg, liquidation cascades)
Operational resilience (DORA-style ICT, third-party, incident response)

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues, Incidents or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe any known weaknesses, prior incidents/exploits, audit findings still open, recent governance disputes, or specific worries.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Single Chainlink feed with no fallback on a thin-liquidity collateral asset; 7-of-11 multisig but 4 signers share one custody provider; top 5 wallets hold 58% of governance token; timelock was reduced to 6h after a contentious vote; front-end hosted on a single cloud region...

exampleInput: We run the core team for an EVM lending protocol live on Ethereum mainnet and two L2s, with about $400m TVL. Governance is a token + an OpenZeppelin Governor with a 48h timelock, but a 4-of-7 multisig (Safe) still holds the proxy admin and can pause markets and change interest-rate and collateral-factor parameters without going through governance. Prices come from Chainlink feeds, with a Uniswap v3 TWAP as a fallback for two long-tail collaterals. The top 6 wallets hold roughly 52% of the governance token (team + two VCs, partly vested). We are pre-launching an EU-facing front-end and want to understand (a) our real operational and governance risk and how to reduce it, and (b) whether we plausibly fall inside or outside MiCA as a 'sufficiently decentralised' service, given the admin keys and the front-end we operate. Known weak spots: no formal verification on the latest rate-model change, the timelock can be bypassed via the multisig pause+upgrade path, and we have no documented incident-response runbook.

exampleValues.known_concerns: 4-of-7 multisig holds proxy admin and can pause + change collateral factors outside governance; timelock bypassable via pause+upgrade path. Top 6 wallets hold ~52% of governance token (team + 2 VCs). Chainlink primary with Uniswap v3 TWAP fallback on two thin-liquidity collaterals — no circuit breaker. No formal verification on latest rate-model change. No documented incident-response runbook.
